userStories.title: Host: context window and subagent event tags
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enrich host state with catalog context-window data and forwarded nested tool events with parent attribution.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — `@/agents/catalog` gains `lookupContextWindow(provider, model)` beside `lookupPricing`, same fail-open contract (undefined on miss, load failure or throw). `ChatHostState` gains `contextWindow?: number`, resolved for the session model (`"<provider>/<model>"`, split at the first `/`; a model string without `/` gets no lookup and no `contextWindow`) when `start`, `resume` and `switchTo` complete, cached per model string; the host calls it through the exported `_chatHostDeps.lookupContextWindow` (default: the catalog function; `export const _chatHostDeps = { lookupContextWindow }` is a new object in `chat-host.ts`, distinct from the `ChatHostDeps` interface). Forwarded subagent `tool_call` / `tool_result` events (`subagent-runs.ts` `routeActivity`) gain `metadata.subagent = agent.qualifiedName` and `metadata.subagentTask = task`, merged over the event's own metadata.

Update host-subagents.test.ts forwarding/spend/late-call assertions to find events by type and callId, assert fixture name/isError plus subagent/subagentTask; the negative lateCall check must assert no forwarded event has that callId. The spend, ledger and text-delta assertions are unchanged. In subagent-runs.test.ts replace toEqual([call,result]) with checks of type/callId/name or isError plus qualified-name/task tags; only those two event types are forwarded, unchanged.

**Scope** — In: catalog lookup, additive host context field/cache/seam, forwarded metadata and affected regression tests. Out: transcript nesting (US-004), context footer (US-017), changes to session/mode/approval or subagent accounting. A per-model `contextWindow` override from config (`models` entries) is not applied to the footer; the catalog value is used.

**Interface** — `lookupContextWindow(provider, model)`; `readonly contextWindow?: number`; `export const _chatHostDeps = { lookupContextWindow }`. Keep ChatHostDeps distinct and preserve the existing ChatHost API.

userStories.title: Tool card results and collapsing
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend tool cards with successful-result summaries, Edit diffs and collapse limits.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** —
- `summary` on ok: Edit -> `Updated <path> (+a -r)` where a and r are the line counts of `new_string` and `old_string`; Write -> `Wrote <n> lines to <path>` (n = line count of `input.content`, a trailing newline not counted); Read -> `Read <k> lines` (k = preview line count) with `+` after k when the preview is at least 4096 bytes (UTF-8) long (the nax-agent preview cap); Bash -> the preview lines, the first `BASH_PREVIEW_LINES` while collapsed with the rest counted in `hiddenLines`; Agent -> `Done (<n> tool uses · <s>s)` (n = children, s = whole seconds from `startedAt` to `endedAt`); any other tool -> its first non-empty preview line, or `Done` for an empty preview. Ok summaries are muted except Bash preview lines, which are plain.
- Line counts: a string's line count is the number of `\n`-separated lines after one trailing `\n` is removed; an empty string has 0 lines.
- `diff`: only an ok Edit has one: `diffLines(old_string, new_string)`, the first `DIFF_PREVIEW_LINES` lines while collapsed (rest in `hiddenLines`).
- `diffLines`: lines common to the start of both texts and lines common to the end become `" "` lines; the remaining old lines become `"-"` lines followed by the remaining new lines as `"+"` lines.
- Expanded: no line limits; an ok Agent also lists every child after its summary.

An ok Bash with an empty preview returns Done. Durations and countdowns from timestamps that do not parse (fixtures use `at: "now"`) count as 0 seconds.

**Scope** — In: extend tool-card.ts and the test file created by US-005. Out: layout/cache (US-010). Line numbers in Edit diffs are not shown; the Edit tool's input carries no start line. A Write approval or tool card does not show the written content as a diff. Subagent tokens are not shown on the Agent card; only tool-use count and duration, because nested usage is not forwarded to the transcript.

**Interface** —
```ts
export function diffLines(oldText: string, newText: string): readonly DiffLine[];
export function toolCardModel(entry: Extract<TranscriptEntry, { kind: "tool" }>, options: { expanded: boolean }): ToolCardModel;
```
Preserve the US-005 model contract and limit constants: TOOL_ARG_LIMIT=60, BASH_PREVIEW_LINES=3, DIFF_PREVIEW_LINES=12, CHILD_PREVIEW_LINES=3.

userStories.title: Markdown: inline styles and blocks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add markdown-to-styled-lines rendering for inline syntax and non-code blocks.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — `markdown.ts`: `renderMarkdown(text, { width, theme }): readonly StyledLine[]`. Parsing uses a maintained markdown lexer and highlighting a maintained highlighter (proposal: the `marked` lexer and the `highlight.js` core build with a registered language set; both are added to `packages/nax/package.json` before the run, see Out of Scope; registered languages: typescript, javascript, json, bash, python, go, rust, yaml, diff, markdown, sql, css, xml, with aliases ts, js, sh, zsh, shell, py, yml, html).

Rendering: headings bold (no `#`); paragraphs word-wrapped to `width`; `**strong**` bold; `*em*` italic; inline code in `accent`; unordered items `- ` (ordered `1. ` in `accent`), nested lists indented two columns per level; blockquotes prefixed by a muted `codeSide` glyph and a space, italic; a horizontal rule is a muted line of the `rule` glyph `width` long; a link renders its text followed by a muted ` (<href>)`;

Tables and raw HTML render as their source text. Malformed markdown (unclosed emphasis, stray fences): Rendered as the lexer tokenises it; never throws.

Every width, wrap and truncation in the models below is measured with `displayWidth`, and a `width` below `MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH` is treated as `MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH`. Every text that comes from the session, a tool, an MCP server or the host (reply, thinking, preview, tool input, notices, listings) passes through `sanitizeText` before it becomes span text, so a tool preview containing `\u001b[?1049l` cannot leave the alternate screen.

**Scope** — In: maintained-lexer inline/block rendering, safe styled text and tests. Out: fenced code and highlighter integration (US-008), transcript indentation/layout (US-009). Adding the markdown lexer and highlighter packages (`marked`, `highlight.js`) to `packages/nax/package.json` and `bun.lock` is done on the feature branch before `nax run`; no story installs packages. Markdown tables are not formatted as aligned columns; they render as their source text.

**Interface** — `renderMarkdown(text, { width, theme }): readonly StyledLine[]`.

userStories.title: Markdown: fenced code and highlighting
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend markdown rendering with framed fenced blocks and fail-open syntax highlighting.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — Parsing uses a maintained markdown lexer and highlighting a maintained highlighter (proposal: the `marked` lexer and the `highlight.js` core build with a registered language set; both are added to `packages/nax/package.json` before the run, see Out of Scope; registered languages: typescript, javascript, json, bash, python, go, rust, yaml, diff, markdown, sql, css, xml, with aliases ts, js, sh, zsh, shell, py, yml, html).

fenced code renders a muted `codeTop` line with the language name, each code line prefixed by a muted `codeSide` and a space, then a muted `codeBottom` line; code lines are not wrapped. A fence with a known language colours tokens by class: keywords and built-ins `syntaxKeyword`, strings `syntaxString`, comments `syntaxComment`, numbers and literals `syntaxNumber`, function and class titles `syntaxTitle`. Unknown or missing language: plain code lines. Tables and raw HTML render as their source text. An unclosed fence (mid-stream) renders as code to the end of the text. The highlighter call goes through the exported `_markdownDeps.highlight` so a test can make it throw.

Highlighter throws for a fence: That fence renders as plain code lines. Apply sanitizeText before span text. Preserve unwrapped long code here; US-009/010 truncate at the layout boundary.

**Scope** — In: fenced blocks, registered languages/aliases, class-to-color conversion and injectable highlighting fallback; extend the US-007 markdown test file. Out: transcript wrapping/cache (US-009/010). Adding the markdown lexer and highlighter packages (`marked`, `highlight.js`) to `packages/nax/package.json` and `bun.lock` is done on the feature branch before `nax run`; no story installs packages. Markdown tables are not formatted as aligned columns; they render as their source text.

userStories.title: Layout: message entries
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add pure transcript layout for user messages, markdown replies and collapsible completed thinking.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — `layout.ts`: `layoutTranscript(entries, { width, theme, expanded }): readonly StyledLine[]`, the concatenation of each entry's lines with one empty line between entries. Per entry:
- `user`: each line of the text prefixed by `> ` (accent) the first and two spaces the rest, every span with background `userBand`.
- `reply`: `renderMarkdown` at `width - 2`, the first line prefixed by the bullet glyph and a space, the rest by two spaces.
- `thinking` without `endedAt`: no lines. With `endedAt`, collapsed: one muted italic line `✻ Thought for <s>s (ctrl+o to show)`; expanded: that line with `(ctrl+o to hide)` and then the thinking text, muted italic, indented two columns.
- Lines longer than `width` are wrapped at word boundaries, continuation lines keeping the entry's indent; a single word longer than the available width is cut at that width; a code line longer than `width` is cut at `width`.
- Durations and countdowns from timestamps that do not parse (fixtures use `at: "now"`) count as 0 seconds.

Every width, wrap and truncation in the models below is measured with `displayWidth`, and a `width` below `MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH` is treated as `MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH`. Every text that comes from the session, a tool, an MCP server or the host (reply, thinking, preview, tool input, notices, listings) passes through `sanitizeText` before it becomes span text, so a tool preview containing `\u001b[?1049l` cannot leave the alternate screen.

**Scope** — In: new layout.ts, message entries, separators, indentation, display-column fitting and tests. Out: tool cards/cache (US-010), welcome/status/listings (US-011), mounting in ChatApp (US-020). Design this entry dispatcher for the full TranscriptEntry union without replacing legacy UI yet.

**Interface** — `layoutTranscript(entries, { width, theme, expanded }): readonly StyledLine[]`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] A user entry with text hi lays out as one line whose plain text is > hi.
[unit] In that line the > span has color accent and every span has background userBand.
[unit] A user entry with text "a\nb" lays out as lines > a and two-spaces b.
[unit] A reply entry with text done lays out as one line whose plain text is the bullet glyph, a space and done.
[unit] A reply whose markdown renders three lines lays out with its second and third lines starting with two spaces.
[unit] A thinking entry without endedAt lays out as zero lines.

userStories.title: Layout: tool cards, listings and the cache
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend transcript layout with tool-card rendering and identity-based per-entry caching.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — `layout.ts`: `layoutTranscript(entries, { width, theme, expanded }): readonly StyledLine[]`, the concatenation of each entry's lines with one empty line between entries.
- `tool`: the line `<bullet> <title>(<arg>)` (`<title>` alone when `arg` is undefined), the bullet coloured `muted`/`success`/`danger` by tone and the arg bold; then the summary lines, the first prefixed `  ⎿  ` (result glyph) and the rest five spaces, coloured by tone; then the diff lines prefixed five spaces, `-` lines with background `diffRemove`, `+` lines with background `diffAdd` (on a theme whose backgrounds are undefined, `-` lines are coloured `danger` and `+` lines `success`); then, when `hiddenLines > 0`, a muted line `     … +<n> lines (ctrl+o to expand)`.
- Lines longer than `width` are wrapped at word boundaries, continuation lines keeping the entry's indent; a single word longer than the available width is cut at that width; a code line longer than `width` is cut at `width`.
- Durations and countdowns from timestamps that do not parse (fixtures use `at: "now"`) count as 0 seconds.
- Caching: the lines of one entry object are computed once per `(width, expanded)` pair; a later call with the same entry object, width and expanded reuses them (`_layoutDeps.layoutEntry` is the injectable per-entry function).

Every width, wrap and truncation in the models below is measured with `displayWidth`, and a `width` below `MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH` is treated as `MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH`. Every text that comes from the session, a tool, an MCP server or the host (reply, thinking, preview, tool input, notices, listings) passes through `sanitizeText` before it becomes span text, so a tool preview containing `\u001b[?1049l` cannot leave the alternate screen.

**Scope** — In: tool-card layout, plain/highlighted code truncation at layout width and the per-entry cache, including caching listing entries when supplied; extend the layout test file from US-009 and preserve its message rendering. Out: defining listing-specific rows and tones (US-011), reducer changes (US-004), keyboard expansion (US-021), Write diffs and Edit line numbers.

**Interface** — `layoutTranscript(entries, { width, theme, expanded }): readonly StyledLine[]`; `_layoutDeps.layoutEntry` is the injectable per-entry function. Cache unchanged entries across calls after reduceTranscript changes only the last reply.

userStories.title: Transcript viewport component
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the Ink transcript viewport over the pure scrolling reducer.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — `TranscriptViewport` renders `height` rows: the visible lines, padded with empty rows at the top while `total < height`, and while `unseen > 0` the last row is replaced by the muted line `↓ <unseen> new lines (End)`. Keys, while its `active` prop is true: pageUp, pageDown, shift+upArrow (lineUp), shift+downArrow (lineDown), home, end.

`offset` counts lines between the bottom of the view and the last line. The reducer's `total` and `height` arguments are the values before the action; a `content` action carries the new ones. Growth (`action.total - total` when positive) while following keeps `offset` 0; while not following it adds the growth to both `offset` and `unseen`. After every action `offset` is re-clamped against the new total and height; a shrink (for example after `/clear`) never makes `unseen` grow.

Render rows through StyledLineView and the supplied theme; wire content/height changes to reduceViewport rather than duplicating the arithmetic.

**Scope** — In: standalone viewport component, active keyboard navigation, unseen indicator and Ink tests. Out: ChatApp height/key ownership wiring (US-020/021). Mouse support (wheel scrolling, click to select) is not added; the screen does not capture the mouse. Searching the transcript and copying from scrolled-off output inside the app are not added; native terminal selection works on what is on screen.

**Interface** — `TranscriptViewport` in `TranscriptViewport.tsx` consumes styled lines, height, theme and an `active` prop; use the US-012 `reduceViewport`/`visibleRange`/`INITIAL_VIEWPORT` contract.

userStories.title: Chat input
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the controlled framed chat input with cursor, multiline draft, in-memory history and clear arming.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — `ChatInput` is controlled: its owner keeps an `InputDraft` (`{ editor: EditorState; history: readonly string[]; browse?: { index: number; saved: EditorState } }`, with `EMPTY_DRAFT`, both exported from `ChatInput.tsx`) and passes `draft` and `onDraftChange`, so unmounting the input while an ask card or a picker is shown loses neither the text nor the history. `ChatInput.tsx` also exports `DOUBLE_ESCAPE_MS` and `_chatInputDeps`. Props: `{ draft: InputDraft; onDraftChange(d: InputDraft): void; onSubmit(text: string): void; width: number; theme: ChatTheme; active?: boolean; busy?: boolean; hint?: string; yieldNavigation?: boolean; onClearArmedChange?(armed: boolean): void }`. With `yieldNavigation` true (the slash menu is open) it ignores up, down, return, tab and escape so the menu owns them. It renders the editor between two full-width rule lines (the `rule` glyph repeated `width` times, coloured `borderFocus` while active, `border` otherwise), the first text row prefixed `> ` (accent), further rows by two spaces, the cursor cell shown in inverse. At most 8 text rows are shown; with more, the 8-row window follows the cursor row. Empty and idle: a muted placeholder `Try "explain how nax run picks a model" · / for commands` (or the `hint` prop when given). History: submitted texts are kept in memory for the component's life; up on the first row recalls the previous entry, down on the last row the next, and moving past the newest restores the draft that was there before browsing. Busy: return submits only when the text starts with `/` (today's rule); otherwise the text stays. Escape on a non-empty idle input arms a clear: a second escape within `DOUBLE_ESCAPE_MS` (2000, timed by the exported `_chatInputDeps.now`) empties it; the component reports the armed state through `onClearArmedChange(armed)`.

Return on whitespace-only input does not submit. Submission empties the editor and retains history in the controlled draft. Use the line-editor reducer; render sanitized text and measure any fitting in display columns with width clamped to MIN_LAYOUT_WIDTH. Preserve the complete placeholder text in the width-20 standalone fixture, as required by its AC, rather than truncating that placeholder to the rule width. Every timer in this feature is a setTimeout chain cleared with clearTimeout on unmount, documented at the call site; setInterval is not used.

**Scope** — In: standalone controlled input and UI tests. Out: owning the ChatApp draft (US-020), ask input composition (US-023), slash-menu selection (US-025). Forward delete (deleting the character under the cursor) is not supported; ink 6.7 reports the Backspace key's `\u007f` and the forward-delete key as the same `delete` key, and both delete before the cursor. Prompt history is not persisted across processes. `@` file mentions and image paste are not added. InputBox keeps serving AskPrompt until US-023.

**Interface** — `InputDraft` = `{ editor: EditorState; history: readonly string[]; browse?: { index: number; saved: EditorState } }`; exported `EMPTY_DRAFT`, `DOUBLE_ESCAPE_MS` = 2000, `_chatInputDeps.now`; props `{ draft: InputDraft; onDraftChange(d: InputDraft): void; onSubmit(text: string): void; width: number; theme: ChatTheme; active?: boolean; busy?: boolean; hint?: string; yieldNavigation?: boolean; onClearArmedChange?(armed: boolean): void }`.

**Goal** — Own alternate-screen lifetime and print the final session summary only after restoring the normal screen.

**Motivation** — The user (2026-10-26) on the current screen: "is really pure text ... make it look like Claude Code or codex", and, after a probe proved both run full screen, "it should keep full same to claude code and codex".

**Goal** — Replace the inline chat presentation with the full-screen header/viewport/working/input/footer composition.

**Motivation** — The user (2026-10-26) on the current screen: "is really pure text ... make it look like Claude Code or codex", and, after a probe proved both run full screen, "it should keep full same to claude code and codex".

Viewport height = `rows - 3 - workingRows - bottomRows - 1`, never below 1. userStories.title: Full-screen ChatApp: keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add escape interruption, transcript expansion/navigation and a live double-interrupt quit hint without changing existing control semantics.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — Keys added: escape while a turn runs calls `host.cancel()` (ctrl-c is unchanged); ctrl+o toggles `expanded`; pageUp, pageDown, shift+up/down, home and end go to the viewport whenever no picker is open. `useChatKeys` gains `quitArmed(): boolean`, true while a ctrl-c that cancelled a turn is less than `DOUBLE_INTERRUPT_MS` old by `_chatKeyDeps.now()`, which the footer reads as the `quit` hint; the first ctrl-c calls `refresh()` and arms a cancellable timer of `DOUBLE_INTERRUPT_MS` that calls `refresh()` again; `finishTurn` disarms it. Every timer in this feature (working-line tick, countdown, quit arm) is a `setTimeout` chain cleared with `clearTimeout` on unmount, documented at the call site; `setInterval` is not used. The footer hint precedence is quit, clear, busy, expanded, idle. Mode cycling, ctrl-c and the busy rules are unchanged. State and handlers may move into hooks (`use-chat-transcript.ts` and the like) to keep `ChatApp.tsx` under the 600-line source limit.

Key ownership (one owner per key and state; the first matching column wins):

| Key | Ask card shown | Picker shown | Slash menu open | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| escape | the card (No) | the picker (cancel) | the menu (close) | turn running: `host.cancel()`; idle: the input's clear-arm |
| return | the card (choose) | the picker (choose) | the menu (run selected) | the input |
| up / down | the card (move) | the picker (move) | the menu (move) | the input (history) |
| tab | nothing | nothing | the menu (complete) | nothing |
| pageUp, pageDown, home, end, shift+up / down | the viewport | nothing | the viewport | the viewport |
| ctrl+o | toggle expanded in every state | | | |
| ctrl-c, shift+tab | `useChatKeys`, unchanged, in every state | | | |

While an ask card is shown, escape never reaches `host.cancel()`. Sending a message after a pageUp shows the newest line. Wire keys into the mounted ChatApp/TranscriptViewport/ChatInput seam rather than isolated helper tests alone. Preserve existing ctrl-c/shift-tab/ask-letter tests.

**Scope** — In: ChatApp key routing, useChatKeys.quitArmed/timer, footer hint precedence, viewport follow reset and mounted UI seams. Out: ask-card implementation (US-023), slash-menu implementation (US-025), pickers (US-027), changing mode cycling or session cancellation/close semantics.

**Interface** — `useChatKeys` adds `quitArmed(): boolean` to existing `locked`, `finishTurn`, `close`, `runControl`; use `_chatKeyDeps.now()` and `DOUBLE_INTERRUPT_MS` (2000). Preserve the existing host control API.

userStories.title: Ask card model
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the pure approval-card model for titles, attribution, options, border tone and Edit diffs.

**Motivation** — The slice 1 acceptance test (brainstorm and spec-review the slice 2 design inside `nax chat`) waits on this redesign.

**Approach** — `ask-card.ts` (pure) and `AskCard.tsx` replace `AskPrompt.tsx`. Approval card: a frame (`warning` border; `danger` when `unsandboxed`), a title, an empty line, the `command` (bold, when present) and the `summary` (muted) indented three columns, the `reason` line, then for Edit the diff of the call (looked up by `callId` in the transcript's tool entries) as in the tool card, then the question and the options, then the countdown. A Write approval or tool card does not show the written content as a diff.
- Title: Bash -> `Bash command`, Edit -> `Edit file`, Write -> `Write file`, Delete -> `Delete file`, a name starting `nax-agents__` -> `Agent`, any other name containing `__` -> `MCP tool <name>`, else the name; plus ` · outside the sandbox` when `unsandboxed`. A reason starting `[agent <name>] ` has that prefix removed from the reason and shown as a muted tag after the title.
- Options: `1. Yes`, `2. Yes, and don't ask again for this in this session` (only when `controller.canRemember(ask)`), and the last `<n>. No, tell nax what to do instead (esc)`. Up/down move the selection, return chooses it, a number key chooses that option, escape chooses No; `a`, `s` (when remembering is allowed) and `d` keep resolving `allow_once`, `allow_session` and `deny`. Ctrl or meta letters do nothing (today's rule).
- Choosing No resolves `deny` and sets the input's hint to `tell nax what to do instead` until the next submit.
- Countdown: muted `expires in m:ss` from `expiresAt` minus now, re-rendered each second through a cancellable timer (`_askCardDeps.now`), `warning` below 60 s.
- Question card: title `nax asks`, the question text, then a `ChatInput` inside the frame with its own `InputDraft`, starting from `EMPTY_DRAFT` for each `requestId` (never the chat input's draft); submit calls `controller.answerQuestion(requestId, text)`.

This story produces the pure model only; component actions/timers above are US-023's boundary. Reuse diffLines from tool-card.ts. Sanitize tool/host reason/summary/command/title/diff strings before they become span text downstream; do not reimplement canRemember policy.

**Scope** — In: askCardModel and unit tests. Out: mounting/keyboard/countdown/answer actions (US-023), changing controller policy or approvals. A Write approval or tool card does not show the written content as a diff. Line numbers in Edit diffs are not shown; the Edit tool's input carries no start line.

**Interface** — `askCardModel` in `ask-card.ts` consumes an approval ask, remembering eligibility and transcript tool entries; returns the title, optional tag, stripped reason, border tone, ordered options and diff. No exact TypeScript declaration is prescribed by the spec; keep the model pure and typed.

[unit] Tool Edit gives title Edit file.
[unit] Tool Write gives title Write file, and tool Delete gives Delete file.

[unit] Tool Grep gives title Grep.

analysis:
Repository exploration used direct reads and text search because the codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this session. This is an enhancement of an existing Bun/TypeScript React/Ink chat, not greenfield. All 28 implementation stories are scoped to packages/nax; nax-agent source is read-only contract context. No-argument /model,/resume,/mode become picker outcomes, with an exhaustive/narrowed ChatApp branch in US-026 before the picker exists. Architecture: implement pure theme/styled text/reducers/card/markdown/layout/status/time/menu models under src/tui/chat plus thin Ink components. Raw HTML/tables are source text, not terminal markup. Durations with unparsable fixture timestamps are zero. The layout must emit only visible lines with one separator between rendered entries; active thinking has no transcript rows.
